confidence_notes: I based the restaurant meal, coffee and beer prices on Numbeo's user-reported prices for Newcastle (Australia), checked against a Numbeo snapshot from June 2026 republished by Expatica. In Australian dollars, that is about A$30 for an inexpensive meal, A$150 for a mid-range meal for two, A$13 for a pint of domestic draft beer and A$5.44 for a cappuccino. For beer I used about A$12, a bit below the pint price, because a standard pub serving in New South Wales is often a schooner. I couldn't find current standard prices for cocktails or wine by the glass. My search found only happy-hour deals (for example, A$14–15 cocktails and A$8 house wine). So I set those prices above the happy-hour levels, using their usual relationship to beer and typical regional New South Wales menus: about A$22 for a cocktail and A$13 for a glass of wine. These two are less certain. The four accommodation prices are my own estimates for July 2026, a winter shoulder season, based on general knowledge. I didn't search for accommodation or look at any booking pages, so these are the least certain anchors. I converted to US dollars at the RBA rate of 0.6720 USD per AUD from 18 November 2026. The pricing window is July 2026, but I used the latest available rate as instructed.
comparable_city_reasoning: Newcastle is a regional coastal city in New South Wales. I assumed restaurant and drink prices slightly below Sydney's and roughly like Wollongong, the Gold Coast or Geelong. I set accommodation below Sydney and closer to other mid-sized Australian coastal cities with moderate tourism and business-travel demand.
